verdict.rationale: Teller says one account connection lets you verify ownership, ACH details, balances, and transactions. It also defines an enrollment as a single bank login that can span multiple accounts, which points to one link session serving several data products. The docs never state outright that balances, transactions, identity and account details all draw from the same enrollment without re-linking, and some institutions need a separate microdeposit flow for account details. Missing for 10: explicit documentation that one enrollment grants access to all products without separate flows, guidance on product or scope selection within Teller Connect, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, one link session can power multiple data products — auth, balances, transactions, identity — without forcing the user through separate connection flows per product

citations.quote: Teller lets users connect their accounts in seconds, and you verify account ownership, ACH details, balances, and transactions with ease.
An enrollment represents one bank login, which may include multiple accounts
Identity provides you with all of the accounts the end-user granted your application access authorization along with beneficial owner identity information for each of them.
